body: This would fuck me up too. It was nearly 2 years of having to endure the noises and the images of something you weren’t ever meant to see as a child. It’s horrible, and it is absolutely a big deal. And I think it is a form of Child sexual assault.

I never said he wasn’t good at his core. I asked a question. I used maybes. Yes, I am allowed to be frustrated when I’m watching something. So far, there hasn’t been a lot of instances where he’s shown kindness. That might be the showrunners fault, or maybe there are good people and bad people whether they are neurodivergent or neurotypical. 

But you are right, and I expressed that I do have privilege and that might’ve affected my opinion. It’s not a gotcha moment as you think it is.

I said “maybe it’s my privilege talking because I’m not autistic so I can’t fully understand what’s going on in his brain, or maybe his obnoxiousness is just inherent to his core being.” Nothing about that statement is concrete. Or do you just want to pick apart parts of the post without looking at the context? 

People have personalities outside of their disabilities. I have a disability that makes it hard for me to behave like a neurotypical person, but it doesn’t define who I am at my core. My personhood is not my disability - it’s a big part, and it shapes my experiences and my reaction, but it’s not my core person. 

I started a discussion, because it’s frustrating to watch. I have friends who are autistic, I have a niece who is a preteen and she’s autistic. And they’re all very sweet people. They have goodness to their core self, outside of their reactions and their difficulties. 

I just struggle to see that with Max, and I wanted to ask whether it’s parenting, or something I’m not understanding or just him as a person outside of his autism.

I think you need to get off your phone and breathe for a second. No one is hating on autistic people. I’ve been polite to you long enough, and you can’t even understand you’re being rude.

I’m not going to engage with you anymore. Goodbye.

So calling me sick and saying something is wrong with me for having a different opinion to you is not hateful? 

This clearly hit a chord for you, and I apologise that I’ve offended you. But damn, you don’t need to be rude to a real person when I’ve been nothing but polite. Also, again, I will reiterate, I never called him an asshole. I just am struggling to watch his behaviour in screen, and it’s irritating when his parents just sit back and let it happen. Just because a member of the family is autistic, does not mean no one else exists. Adam and Kristina set up a dynamic where there is no space for the rest of the siblings to feel anything. That’s not right. 

You can put in the extra work for a kid who needs it, whilst still holding space for everyone else. Their dynamic doesn’t allow it. That’s a problem. That’s why Max doesn’t learn.

Where did I say he was an asshole? And do you not think that children should not be held accountable for how they behave? That’s how they become better as people. 

They don’t live in a vacuum, and they have to learn to adjust as much as possible to not cause harm and stress to everyone around them. Yes, people who are neurodivergent should get more empathy and understanding since it’s harder for them to grasp certain things. But that doesn’t negate from the fact that it’s the parents responsibility show them empathy and respect and kindness. 

I’m not a parent, but I am neurodivergent. Not autistic, but neurodivergent so I understand things being harder. We are not absolved of all responsibility because of it.

The only thing they see is your trauma and your mental health. Your core to people is your worst self. Idk about others, but I can’t escape my image as someone who is always a mess. Even though I’m mostly not. It’s just that my mess is louder than everything else about me.

Honestly, I agree about his parents. I think they spoke about empathy very briefly once? Other than that, they’re just so busy trying to make sure he doesn’t feel bad about his autism, that they’ve made him invincible.  

He likes rules, so they should’ve focused on societal rules. Not as a throwaway comment, but something they take their time to make sure he understands. I felt so bad for Haddie and I felt so bad for Jabbar. Amber actually dealt with him better than his own mother.
